subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@astertech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Discovery recap: Multi-tenancy controls & rate limits

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Tenant "noisy neighbor" spikes are causing tail-latency issues for other customers.
- Need per-customer rate limiting and monthly quotas for billing and abuse mitigation.
- Want routing policies so premium customers hit a dedicated pool (or higher-priority nodes) during bursts.
- Need auditability: per-tenant logs, quota usage reports, and alerts on quota breaches.

Current stack and constraints you told us:
- API gateway in front of an internal inference cluster (K8s).
- Approximately ~50 tenants today; ~10 are "large" and drive most spikes.
- Billing is currently invoice-based; engineering wants usage buckets to enable tiered billing.

Success criteria for a POC (your priorities):
1) Enforce per-tenant QPS and short-term burst limits with minimal added latency.
2) Per-tenant monthly token quotas surfaced to billing.
3) Routing policy to route VIP tenant traffic to dedicated capacity during spikes.
4) Audit logs and simple dashboards for quota/usage per tenant.

What Redwood can provide / quick notes:
- We support tenant-scoped rate limits and quotas (configurable by route or header).
- Routing by tenant id is supported — you can map tenants to pools or priority tiers.
- Out-of-the-box telemetry includes per-tenant token usage, tail-latency percentiles, and quota breach alerts.
- We can run a 2–3 week POC using a dedicated pool + canary routing to validate isolation.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send our security questionnaire and a short POC plan (attached).
2) Rishi (cc'd) will follow up with high-level commercial options for a dedicated pool.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Laura Bennett (solutions engineer) to validate integration points (headers/auth, routing keys).

Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf, redwood-sla-draft.pdf

Thanks — available to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samir Patel <samir@astertech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@astertech.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Multi-tenancy controls & rate limits

Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap, that captures things well. A couple clarifications and ask from our side:

Clarifications:
- We have ~50 tenants today, yes; 8–12 customers regularly spike and cause disrupted SLAs for others.
- Desired quotas: per-tenant monthly token budget (for billing) + per-second QPS caps with short burst windows.
- Routing: ideally premium customers route to a reserved pool of nodes in peak, fallback to shared if reserved capacity is saturated.

Asks:
1) Can you share SOC2 or security attestation (or point me to where we can find it)? Our security team will need it before a POC.
2) Ballpark pricing for a dedicated pool for the POC (we're thinking a 2–3 week run with a single reserved node set).
3) A sample of the per-tenant usage/metrics dashboard would help get our finance folks comfortable.

We can do the technical deep dive next week — mornings PT work best for Laura/our infra lead.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Infrastructure | AsterTech
samir@astertech.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@astertech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Multi-tenancy controls & rate limits

Thanks Samir —

Quick answers inline and next steps:

1) SOC2 / security attestation: attaching the security questionnaire and our SOC2 excerpt. If your security team needs a call with our security lead we can set that up this week.

2) Pricing for POC: for a short 2–3 week POC we typically offer a standard dedicated pool configuration. Rishi will send two commercial flavors (trial credit + paid reserved node) — ballpark, expect a single reserved 8-GPU node equivalent to be in the $Xk/week range depending on burst capacity.

3) Dashboards: we’ll share a sample dashboard (attached) that shows per-tenant tokens, QPS, latency p95/p99, and quota breach events.

Technical notes:
- Tenant id can be passed via header (X-Redwood-Tenant) or within token introspection.
- Rate limits are enforced at the routing/proxy level and again at the serving runtime for safety — this keeps enforcement low-latency.
- Routing policies: you can define static routing rules (tenant -> pool) and dynamic policies (route premium when shared pool CPU > 75%).

Next steps:
- Laura to run a 60-min technical session next Tue/Wed morning PT to validate integration.
- Rishi to share a POC commercial note + preliminary contract bullets.
- Samir / Leah to share a short list of 3 tenants you’d like in the POC and expected traffic patterns.

Attachments: redwood-architecture-sketch.pdf

Laura — are mornings next Tue/Wed PT good for a 60-min dial-in?

Best,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@astertech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Multi-tenancy controls & rate limits

Samir —

Looping in on commercial next steps. Appreciate the alignment here — we’ll draft a short POC addendum that includes: scope (2–3 weeks), objectives (isolation + quota reporting), success criteria, and an optional conversion path to a reserved capacity commit.

Can you confirm availability for a kickoff technical session on Tue 23 Jun 2026 10:00 AM PT / Wed 24 Jun 2026 10:00 AM PT (either works for us; pick what suits your infra folks).

Also sharing a quick note on pricing options in a separate email — Marissa will attach the POC plan and the security artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.
